FST correctly produces bugun (Lautgesetzlich early-OE / Mercian outcome of cogset row 1962 *búgun, 3pl pret. of *beuganą "to bow"); the -un>-on lowering is phonologically blocked here because OEMedUnstressedULowering (germanic.txt:2298) has a left-context exclusion [EnglishStarVocalic - [{*u}|{*ū}|{*ú}]], parallel to the stem-u + single-C harmony environment that protects wuduwe / munuc / duguþ (Brunner §44 Anm. 7; Luick §326.2). Attested lWS bugon is an analogical overlay levelling on the dominant 3pl pret. -on ending of other strong-verb classes (ridon, bundon, drifon, wǣron) (Campbell §735(e); Brunner §364.2 Anm. 4). Cross-Germanic confirms -un preservation (OS budun, dribun, wurdun) and Ép./VP/Ru.1 show -un dominant for class-II verbs; but no -un form survives for būgan/ābūgan/onbūgan/gebūgan in the OE corpus — every locatable 3pl pret. token (Chronicle 901/919/959/999/1086, Ælfric, Wulfstan, Gregory's Dialogues, Maldon 185) shows -on, so bugun is paradigm-regular but type-unattested.
